title: THE KINGDOMS THAT RISE AND FALL

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Edom will be conquered; Seir, his enemy, will be conquered, but Israel will grow strong. A ruler will come out of Jacob and destroy the survivors of the city." - Num 24:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam's vision continues, foretelling the fall of Edom and the strength of Israel. A ruler would come out of Jacob who would prevail over his enemies. These were specific words about the nations surrounding Israel and the future God had determined for them in the unfolding of history.

We should read these as words about real nations in a particular time, part of God's dealings with Israel and the peoples around them. They remind us that God governs the rise and fall of nations. Kingdoms that seem permanent will pass away, while God's purposes stand firm. History moves according to His hand.

Behind the mention of a ruler from Jacob lies, once again, the shadow of the greater King. Every earthly ruler God raised up from Israel pointed toward the ultimate Ruler, the Messiah who would establish a kingdom that would never fall. The nations rise and fade, but His reign endures forever.

This teaches us where to place our confidence. Not in earthly powers, which come and go, but in the everlasting kingdom of Christ. Nations may rise in strength and crumble into dust, but the Ruler from Jacob reigns eternally. In a world of shifting powers, anchor your hope in the King whose throne will never be shaken (Dan 7:14).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted to trust in earthly powers that will not last?
2. How does God's rule over nations shape the way you view world events?
3. What does it mean to anchor your hope in Christ's everlasting kingdom?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You govern the rise and fall of every nation. Keep me from trusting in powers that fade, and anchor my hope in the everlasting kingdom of Christ, the Ruler from Jacob. Amen.
